title: Decision Lane: guided rollout composer and rollback decisioning
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: PMs and platform engineers need a single, guided interface to compose multi-strategy releases (canary + A/B + shadow) while keeping rollback decisioning explicit and auditable. Current composer screens are fragmented: users create separate canaries, manual traffic splits, and then rely on disparate dashboards to decide to roll back. This increases cognitive load and slows incident response.

Goal: Design a "Decision Lane" composer that: 1) lets users build a multi-lane release plan (e.g., Canary lane, A/B lane, Shadow lane, Emergency lane) in one visual canvas, 2) exposes safety gates and signal thresholds inline, 3) surfaces a compact rollback decision helper with diffs and suggested mitigations, 4) records the final decision + rationale for audit logs.

Scope: UX prototype for the composer canvas + rollback helper popover, a playbook panel with suggested safety templates, and a compact compare/rollback lane that supports immediate emergency actions. Not covering backend rollout engine or telemetry ingestion (ENG dependency).

Design highlights: Decision Lanes are horizontal bands representing traffic strategies. Each lane has: name, percentage (or shadow flag), prerequisite gates, staged timers, signal monitors (latency/error/quality), and a confidence meter. Users can link lanes with conditional rules (e.g., promote to 50% if error increase < 0.5%). Rollback helper shows: baseline vs candidate diffs (latency/cost/quality), recent alert hits, and a suggested rollback action (full rollback, partial reduce, switch to fallback model).

Trade-offs and constraints considered: - Minimalist default: present 1-2 canned templates for quick safety, but allow deep custom rules for power users. - Avoid clutter: inline gates collapsed by default, expanded on hover/click. - Mobile/compact view: provide a condensed timeline view for on-call usage. - Accessibility: keyboard-first lane reordering and clear color contrast for lanes and health states.

Acceptance criteria (high level): - Prototype demonstrates creating a 3-lane plan and linking a gate-based rule. - PMs/Eng reviewers can simulate signal changes and see suggested rollback actions. - UX includes an audit card that captures decision rationale and links to the release event.

Success metrics: - Decrease mean time to rollback by 20% in pilot orgs. - >80% of pilot users can complete a 3-lane plan within 4 minutes in unmoderated tests.

Notes: This ticket focuses on design explorations and prototype validation. Backend contract is tracked in ENG-21002. Coordinate with PM for acceptance tests and with Research for user session recruitment.
comments: 2025-11-12 - Ava Martinez: Initial draft of Decision Lane concept posted; Figma proto links attached. Asked for early ENG/PM signals on what metrics are guaranteed in the first rollout (latency, 5xx, model-quality score).
2025-11-14 - Priya Desai (PM): Requested we include a 'canary cool-down' timer and tie the UI to the console's incident view. Also suggested an emergency lane template for immediate rollback actions.

2025-11-16 - Marco Liu (Eng): Noted dependency ENG-21002 for rollout API v2. Need a compact JSON spec for lane rules to validate prototype flows. Also flagged metric latency (per-route) availability in dedicated/private could lag; propose graceful degradation UI state.

2025-11-18 - Design critique (team): Feedback from design review: expand the rollback helper to include a simple cost delta estimate and a signal provenance callout (which dashboard/alert fired). Revise visual cadence to avoid overuse of red; use amber + clear text labels for degraded states.
2025-11-20 - Liam O'Connor: Updated prototype with collapsible gate rows, added keyboard reordering. Poked at assistive text for lane icons. Ready for PM review and scheduling a usability session.
2025-11-20 - QA note (TBD): Need to define scenario scripts for simulated signal injections; will add after ENG confirms mock telemetry endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Create a multi-lane plan (canary + A/B + emergency) on the canvas and save as a release plan.
Simulate a signal breach and have the rollback helper present at least two actionable suggestions.
Audit card captures the selected rollback action, user comment, and timestamp; linkable from release history.
Prototype supports keyboard-only reordering and lane collapsing for accessibility testing.
design_notes: Lane visualization: compact lane header with name, icon, percent, confidence pill; expanded view shows gates and rules.
Rollback helper: three-pane micro view: (1) summary diff, (2) recent alerts and signal chart sparkline, (3) action buttons with one-click emergency rollback.
Safety templates live in a side panel; users can drag a template onto the canvas to instantiate lanes.
Telemetry caveat: if signal is not available for a lane, show 'signal unavailable' and gray out automated promotion controls.
next_steps: Schedule 3 remote usability sessions with platform PMs and SREs (Research to coordinate).
Align with ENG-21002 to finalize the lane rules JSON contract; get a mocked telemetry endpoint for prototype testing.
Polish Figma prototype based on design critique notes and re-run internal demo on 2025-11-24.
Prepare acceptance test checklist for PM and QA once ENG provides test harness.
